# Relative prices and measured productivity by sector — Latin America and the Caribbean

*Generated by `empirics/code/lp/09_baumol.py`; do not edit by hand (D-043).*

Change in each sector's productivity relative to the economy-wide average, at current prices, split exactly into a real part (constant 2020 prices) and a relative-price part. Log points per year; ILO modelled employment; official total value added as the denominator.

## 1. Low-productivity sectors, 2000–2019: medians across countries (excluding Cuba, Venezuela (Bol. Rep. of))

Sectors whose value added per worker at current prices was below the economy-wide average in 2000.

| Sector | Countries | Relative productivity, current prices | = real | + relative price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agriculture, forestry, fishing | 25 | +0.56 | +0.95 | -0.05 |
| Manufacturing | 8 | +0.69 | +0.16 | +0.65 |
| Construction | 19 | +0.25 | -0.80 | +0.59 |
| Trade, restaurants and hotels | 26 | -0.32 | -0.47 | +0.23 |
| Transport, storage and communication | 2 | -1.01 | -0.37 | -0.63 |
| Other services (finance, business, government, personal) | 3 | +0.52 | +0.22 | +0.56 |

Medians of each column are taken separately, so they need not add up.

## 2. Baumol slope: relative-price change on real relative-productivity change

Pooled across countries and sectors (mining and utilities excluded). Cost disease predicts a slope near −1.

| Period | Observations | Countries | Slope | 90% interval (country bootstrap) | Correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1991–2000 | 162 | 27 | -0.42 | [-0.64, -0.18] | -0.43 |
| 2000–2008 | 162 | 27 | -0.38 | [-0.51, -0.23] | -0.41 |
| 2008–2019 | 162 | 27 | -0.37 | [-0.54, -0.18] | -0.42 |
| 2019–2024 | 162 | 27 | -0.27 | [-0.44, -0.18] | -0.51 |
| 2000–2019 | 162 | 27 | -0.48 | [-0.62, -0.29] | -0.55 |

Measurement error pulls the slope in both directions. An error in a sector's employment moves its real and nominal relative productivity together and leaves the relative-price term unchanged, so it biases the slope toward zero. An error in a sector's deflator moves the real and relative-price terms in opposite directions and biases the slope toward −1 (OQ-59).
